The test image shows a soybean field that is predominantly green but with visible scattered yellowing throughout the canopy. The yellowing appears more pronounced in the lower/middle canopy areas, with some patches of yellow-green discoloration mixed in with the healthy green tissue.

Comparing to the Septoria_brown_spot reference images: the top-right panel shows a very similar field-level view — mostly green plants with scattered yellowing beginning in the lower canopy, matching the test image closely. Septoria brown spot characteristically progresses from lower to upper canopy with angular brown spots causing rapid yellowing and defoliation.

The scattered yellowing pattern visible across the rows in the test image is consistent with Septoria brown spot disease progression, not a more dramatic whole-plant collapse (ruling out Phytophthora, Sudden Death Syndrome) and not the white/cottony growth of White Mold.
